title: [Task Sprint] QA Testing Report — GoThru 360 Viewer

issues.display_title: Issue #10: Fix Issue Google Drive Connection Doesn't Work
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

albug — 7:55 PM
One thing that doesn't work is the Google drive connection
On both apps

Google Drive backup (sign-in / connect) fails for the tester on both apps. Since it reproduces on both, the cause is almost certainly server-side OAuth configuration in Google Cloud rather than platform code.

Where it lives

Piece File
Drive service — sign-in, folder, rsync, resumable upload lib/services/drive_backup.dart
Riverpod state + backup loop lib/state/backup_providers.dart
Local mirror of what's on Drive (Hive) lib/data/backup_store.dart
Backup screen (select-all + per-image) lib/views/backup_screen.dart
Per-image entry point lib/views/asset_actions.dart
iOS OAuth client id + URL scheme ios/Runner/Info.plist
Setup notes GOOGLE_DRIVE_SETUP.md

GCP project: silicon-topic-858. Scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file (non-sensitive).

Suspected root causes (ranked)

1. OAuth consent screen is still in Testing — affects BOTH apps ⚠️ most likely

GOOGLE_DRIVE_SETUP.md records the consent screen as Testing, which means:

  • Only email addresses explicitly added as test users can sign in at all. Anyone else gets blocked ("app has not completed verification" / access_denied) — this alone would make Drive fail on both Android and iOS for a tester who isn't on the list.
  • Refresh tokens expire after 7 days, so even allow-listed testers get silently kicked out roughly weekly.

The code already has a workaround for the second symptom — DriveBackup._isReauthCanceled retries once on Credential Manager's [16] Account reauth failed — which is a strong hint this is already biting in practice.

Fix: flip the consent screen to Production. Because drive.file is non-sensitive this needs no Google security assessment — only the basic branding/support-email fields.

2. Android OAuth client SHA-1 is stale — affects Android only

The Android OAuth client is registered with only the debug keystore SHA-1:

A9:84:94:7E:83:B8:DC:B0:75:AF:4C:56:10:E4:04:D7:93:84:8A:0F

GOOGLE_DRIVE_SETUP.md justifies that with "the release build currently signs with the debug config too" — that is no longer true. android/app/build.gradle.kts now signs release with the upload keystore from android/key.properties, and Play App Signing re-signs with a third key on top:

signingConfig = if (hasReleaseKeystore) {
    signingConfigs.getByName("release")
} else {
    signingConfigs.getByName("debug")
}

Android's Credential Manager authenticates by package name + SHA-1. Any build not signed with the debug key therefore fails with ApiException: 10 (DEVELOPER_ERROR) — which the app surfaces as the generic "Google sign-in failed. Please try again."

Fix: add both missing SHA-1s to the Android OAuth client:

  • the upload keystore's SHA-1 (keytool -list -v -keystore <upload.jks> -alias <alias>)
  • the Play App Signing SHA-1 from Play Console → Setup → App integrity

3. iOS config — verified consistent, deprioritized

Checked and matching, so probably not the iOS cause:

  • PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = co.360viewer.gothru (note: no "u" — deliberately differs from Android's co.u360viewer.gothru)
  • GIDClientID = ...-ia2vs2csb04sabkku3c5anps8ekkea1u.apps.googleusercontent.com
  • reversed client id present in CFBundleURLSchemes

Still worth confirming the iOS OAuth client in GCP is registered against Team ID W433ZFZCX5 and that bundle id.

4. Errors are unreadable — blocks diagnosis either way

BackupController._message() collapses every non-cancel/non-interrupt GoogleSignInException into one string:

default:
  return 'Google sign-in failed. Please try again.';

The Google status code (10 / 12500 / 16) and description are dropped, so a tester's report can't distinguish SHA-1 mismatch from an unverified-app block from a network failure. That is why this report arrives as "doesn't work" with nothing actionable attached.

Acceptance criteria

  • Reproduce and capture the real error on Android (adb logcat / GoogleSignInException code) and on iOS
  • Add the upload-keystore SHA-1 and the Play App Signing SHA-1 to the Android OAuth client in GCP project silicon-topic-858
  • Verify the iOS OAuth client's bundle id + Team ID, and that the Drive API is enabled on the project
  • Move the OAuth consent screen from Testing to Production (no security assessment needed for drive.file)
  • Surface the underlying Google error code/description in the snackbar (or at minimum log it) instead of the generic "Google sign-in failed"
  • End-to-end verify on a release build from Play (not just a debug build): sign in → GoThru folder created → photo + video upload → rsync skips already-uploaded assets on a second run
  • Verify the same flow on a TestFlight/release iOS build
  • Update GOOGLE_DRIVE_SETUP.md — the "release signs with the debug config" note is now stale, and record the final publishing status

Notes

  • The Testing-mode 7-day expiry means this bug can appear fixed and silently regress a week later. Confirm the fix after Production is live, not before.
  • Uploads consume each user's own 15 GB Drive quota; the Drive API itself is free, so this is not a billing/quota-exhaustion issue on our side.

issues.display_title: Issue #13: Connect 360 Viewer App to Panorra for Direct Publishing
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A feature request has been submitted to integrate the Panorra platform directly into the GoThru 360 Viewer mobile app.

Currently, users lack a direct bridge between these two services within the mobile environment. We need to build a connection that allows users to seamlessly publish their 360 content directly from the 360 Viewer app straight to Panorra, streamlining their workflow.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. A "Publish to Panorra" option is clearly visible and accessible for content within the GoThru 360 Viewer app.
  2. Users can successfully authenticate or link their Panorra accounts through the mobile app.
  3. Initiating a publish action from the app successfully transfers the 360 content and makes it live on the user's Panorra account.
  4. The app gracefully handles any network or API errors, displaying readable error messages to the user if the publish action fails.

issues.display_title: Issue #17: Hanlde Issue Panorra Authentication Failing with Generic Error in 360 Viewer
issues.main_description_html:
Feedback

Description

Users are reporting an inability to connect their Panorra accounts within the GoThru 360 Panorama Viewer app.

When attempting to sign in on the Panorra integration screen, the login fails and the app displays a generic red error banner: "Something went wrong. Please try again." This issue blocks users from utilizing the Panorra direct publishing feature.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the GoThru 360 Panorama Viewer mobile app.
  2. Navigate to the section to connect or publish to Panorra, opening the "Sign in to Panorra" screen.
  3. Attempt to authenticate using email/password or the Google SSO option.
  4. Actual Result: The authentication fails, and the generic error message appears above the input fields.
  5. Expected Result: The app successfully authenticates the credentials and links the user's Panorra account.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Users can successfully authenticate and connect to Panorra from within the 360 Panorama Viewer app.
  2. If a login attempt fails for a legitimate reason (e.g., incorrect password, network timeout), the app displays a specific, descriptive error message rather than a generic fallback.

DEVELOPER REPORT

Issue:
Users signing in to Panorra via "Continue with Google" could fail to sign in. The cause was that the publish-to-Panorra feature was using an incorrect Google authentication ID, different from the one used by other Google Sign-In features in the app.

Fixing:
The Google authentication ID for Panorra has been corrected to use the same credentials already working reliably in other features (Drive backup, Street View publishing).
